author: phylliswebb19987
desc: Why It Sucks to Be a Concubine (in Ancient Egypt)#Concubine #animation
transcript: Afterward, you lie on a cedar scented mat and stare at the ceiling where a painted hunting scene loops in bright color. You find the cat in the painting and you stare at it until morning. You decide not to think too much. Thinking too much will only open something you cannot close. Days become weeks. Weeks become a pattern. You learn the pattern and you keep your face smooth. The older women say a smooth face is your greatest tool. They say this without pity, which is almost its own kind of pity. Then one morning, you cannot eat the bread. Your stomach turns at the smell of the oil. The mistress of the household watches your face over her clipboard of accounts. She sends for a physician. He is a priest doctor who smells of natron and old incense. He presses your wrist, checks your eyes, asks you questions in that flat, professional voice. He tells the mistress something in a low tone. The mistress nods. You are pregnant. The house shifts around you like a current changing direction. Your food portions double. A servant is assigned to walk with you in the garden. Mornings and evenings the lady of the house visits your chamber, which she has never done before. She stands in the doorway and looks at your stomach with an expression that is not quite hatred and not quite grief, but lives somewhere in between them. Then she leaves without speaking. That look will live. In you longer than the visit. You ask your mother in your mind, to put her hands on you. She doesn't answer because she is 100 miles south and doesn't know where you are.

author: rules3am
transcript: Dashboard says rear seatbelts two. Most of you said stay. And some of you noticed she did blink at the start. It's 309:00am. Mrs. Carter drove right past your house. Dad's text said, get out. You stay. The door is still open. Cold air pours in. The middle seat sinks slowly, like someone just sat down. Close the door, sweetheart. I got in because you listen to him. Then your phone rings. Not a text, a call. The caller ID says dad with his photo. Some of you found it. The texts came from an unknown number. Dad? Kiddo, where are you? I'm at the hospital. Mrs. Carter is here with me. She's been here all night. Slowly, you look at the driver seat. Same sweater, same smile. Still not blinking. Hang up, sweetheart. The screen flickers. What's our family password? Only you and dad know it. You made it up together. You never told anyone. Then from the middle seat, something whispers it right into your ear. In your own voice. Pumpkin pie.

desc: Weird History Stories You Didn't Know  #2danimation #animation #history
transcript: Union Cannonball crashes through the kitchen and lands in Wilmer's fireplace. As most sensible people would, he looks at the gaping hole in his kitchen wall, looks back at the Cannonball, and starts to think, you know, this war thing ain't for me. At the time, he had no idea that the cannonball he was staring at was the first shot fired of the American Civil War at what would be later known as the battle of Bull Run. Wilmer decides to do the best thing he can do to get away from the fighting. He purchases a property roughly 120 miles south in another part of Virginia and hits the road with his family. They travel for days, each mile feeling a little safer and just that little bit farther from a war that found its way to his doorstep. They move into their new home, and finally, they're safe for now. The war that everyone thought was going to be a quickie drags on and becomes the bloodiest conflict in American history. Four years pass, and though they had won many of the initial conflicts in the war, by 1865, the Confederacy was hanging on by a thread. In April of that year, Confederate general Robert E. Lee is being pursued by union troops LED by Ulysses S. Grant. Reached the town of Appomattox, Virginia, starving, having marched without food for days. Hoping for just a moment to catch their breath. They're almost immediately found by Grant's men, who Surround them outside the town courthouse, General Lee realizes that the game is up. Rather than send his men to die, he decides to surrender. He looks around the town for a nice house that would be a suitable place to end the war. They find one to their liking, and Lee and grant approach the house together and knock on the door. You gotta be fucking kidding me. The two generals ask Wilmer if they can use his living room to sign the documents that would certify General Lee surrender. He reluctantly agrees, and his home is once again filled with Civil War troops. At least nothing comes crashing through the wall this time. But maybe it's even worse. transcript: During World War 2, one of Japan's most celebrated naval commanders climbed aboard a plane to inspect his troops. And ran straight into a pack of American fighter jets right in his own backyard. They shot him right out of the sky. That unlucky commander was Yamamoto Isoroku, heart and soul of the Japanese Navy in World War 2. He was the man who LED Japan's combined fleet on a rampage across the Western Pacific and Southeast Asia. He was also the mastermind behind the attack on Pearl Harbor, the battle of midway, and a string of other major operations. Maybe it was precisely because he was so good that fate decided to play a little joke on him. In April 1943, after Japan's catastrophic defeat at Guadalcanal, Yamamoto decided to visit the front lines in person to boost troop morale. The plan was to board a transport plane from Rabaul airbase and fly out to Bougainville Island to arrange the reception. The Japanese navy sent Yamamoto's itinerary to all the bases along the route. But that telegram had barely gone out before American forces intercepted it. So what do you all think about this telegram? This guy is the one who planned Pearl Harbor. Take him out. My thoughts exactly. But if we shoot him down, we're basically telling Japan their codes are broken. That's a fair point. So we just pretend we never saw the telegram? Joking. Just joking. Forget I said anything. What if we say we just happened to Be in the area and we accidentally shot him down. Accidentally in the area? How do you even come up with that? The Japanese aren't children. Great idea. And just like that, the plan that someone laughed at got approved. On the morning of April 18th, Yamamoto's flight departed Rabil Airbase right on schedule. At the same exact time, more than a dozen American P38 Lightning fighters took off from Guadalcanal. According to the attack plan, the formation was split into two groups. The lead planes went straight for Yamamoto's transport, while the planes behind them peeled off to draw away the Japanese escort fighters. To avoid the radar stations on Japanese held islands along the route, the American formation took a wide detour around the south side. After several hours of flying, two sides met over Bougainville Island. Right on cue, the American fighters immediately went straight for Yamamoto's flight. After a few exchanges, the right engine of the plane carrying Yamamoto was hit. The aircraft nosed straight down into the jungle of Bougainville and exploded on impact. By the time the Japanese search and rescue team reached the crash site, Yamamoto was already dead.

desc: Why It Sucks to Be a Geisha (in Meiji Japan) #historytime #animation #2danimation #fyp #why
transcript: inside your thoughts go far away the experience itself is not dramatic it is worse than that it is hollow mechanical something endured rather than lived you focus on the ceiling beams on the way your breath sounds too loud in your own ears you even try to console yourself with the knowledge that this moment this transaction will be recorded as a success when it ends he leaves with white satisfaction you remain there numb afterward nothing looks different in the corridors of the okiya the same floors the same paper walls the same rules but you are no longer addressed as before your name appears more often on guest lists your sleeves grow longer and your rank improves people congratulate you you are told you are fortunate you are treated with more respect but more caution you are invited where you were once excluded men look at you differently not as a promise but as a possession with credentials you realize you are no longer a child not because you chose to grow up but because your body has been converted into value as the years go by you bloom fully into your womanhood at 23 your name is requested before others tea houses adjust their evenings around your availability you no longer wait in the anteroom you are announced at banquets you sit perfectly straight for hours you laugh at the right moments you remember who prefers dry socket and who likes flattery disguised as wit the clients are different now the samurai are gone their stipends dissolved into history in their place come businessmen ministry officials and industrialists who smell of ink coal and new money they bring gifts a lacquered comb from Osaka a silk obi dyed in colors you've never seen before imported chocolates wrapped in paper you cannot read none of them belong to you the okiya owns it all one foreign client returns often taller than the others his Japanese rough but enthusiastic he asks again and again if you will go back with him to his country he speaks of freedom you smile and refuse politely you have heard what happens to women who accept rumors of how they vanish into circuses your image circulates too a photographer poses you beneath painted cherry blossoms these photographs appear on postcards sold to travelers you hear foreigners buy them by the stack you never see the money you are told it goes toward expenses you did not approve it is at your peak you understand the truth clearly while your fame has grown your choices have not you are admired displayed circulated and still indebted you realize visibility is not ownership of the self prestige is

And begins setting his sights on larger conquests. He soon realizes that the greatness he desires will be impossible if he's still under the thumb of his grandfather, and he begins plotting ways to regain Purge's independence. Back in Medea, Harpagus gets wind that Cyrus may have higher ambitions, and he sends him a secret message. In his letter, he reminds Cyrus of how his grandfather wanted him killed, and that if Persia were to lead a rebellion against Medea, he would turn his forces against the Stygies and fight alongside him. This sounds like a pretty good deal, but Cyrus has one last problem. Persia is less of a kingdom and more of a scattering of tribes that kind of tolerate a ruler. transcript: Stop the party! Stop it! Hey! Hey, what's the matter? It's Henry. Henry? What happened to Henry? He. His body had been discovered in the woods near the highway. The cops said Henry had been stabbed 15 times. No, no, no. That's not possible. What the hell are you saying? The cops found his punctured car on the highway. Seems like his attacker trapped him and lured him into the woods and then killed him. I dropped the glass on the floor and rushed to the washroom. Henry came to the party with me. There's no way what Gary's saying is true. The washroom is empty. Henry. Henry. I kept saying his name. Suddenly, my eyes went to the mirror on my left, and I saw him. Henry was looking at me from the top of an open bathroom stall. I could see his head floating above the stall, and the stall was more than eight feet tall. In the reflection of the mirror, Henry smiled. And then his face vanished in the thin air. The hair on my body stood up as I realized what the sounds from the woods meant when I met Henry. It was Henry's killer stabbing him in the distance. I still don't know if it was Henry's spirit or if the entire thing was my hallucination. But the story gets even creepier from here. One week later, Gary called me. The cops found Henry's killer. They did? Good. I hope that freak rots in Jail. He won't. What do you mean, he won't? He killed Henry. What other reason the guy was found dead? What? I couldn't speak after that. Gary went on to say that the man's name was Warner. He was a drug dealer as well as a notorious thief. The night he killed Henry, he ran away into the woods to escape the cops. But the next morning, the cops found him dead in the creek. Do you think Henry took his revenge?
